To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the level of carbamylation of HbA is significantly increased in uremic patients and the level of glycation of HbA in diabetic patients.
we have separated and quantitated two new minor hemoglobin components, HbA1D3A and HbAID3B, that are increased in uremic or diabetic patients respectively.

two new minor hemoglobin species, HbA1dc and HbAld3, are present in the blood of uremic and diabetic individuals and that they are useful markers for the assessment of long-term uremia or hyperglycemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the heterogeneity of HbA(1c) in uremic and diabetes mellitus.
the heterogeneity of HbA(1d) which is the main component of HbA(fast) (HbA1).
the characterization of minor hemoglobins and the development of a new method for their quantification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HbA1 level, as a whole, is the sum of HbA0, HbA1a, HbA2, HbA3, HbA4 and HbA5, and the level of each minor hemoglobin is a specific index reflecting the metabolic status of the patient.
the carbamylation of hemoglobin is a major cause of the increased level of Hb A1d3 in uremic patients.
HbA3 is the sum of HbA3, HbA1, HbA2, HbA3a and Hba3b.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
carbamylated HbA1 is the major hemoglobin modified by carbamyation and glycation is the major hemoglobins modified by glycation in uremic and in diabetic patients, respectively.
the HbA1 level in uremic or diabetic patients is a combination of HbA0, HbA1a and two new minor hemoglobin components, HbAld3a and HblAld3b.

the two new minor hemoglobin variants, HbA1D3a and Hba1d3b are useful as markers for the evaluation of long-term uremia or glycemia in uremia and diabetic patients, and the quantification of these two hemoglobins can be easily achieved with high precision using the capillary zone electrophoresis method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantitation of HbA3d and HbA3b can be a useful complement to HbA(1c) and carbamylated Hb in the objective assessment of uremia and diabetes, respectively.
HbA(1d) can be a useful marker for glycemic control.
the HbA1C assay is not a good indicator of glycemic control in uremic patients, as uremic patients have higher levels of HbA2 and carbamylated Hb than non-uremic subjects.
